title: Kinesis vs MSK streaming design
scenario: Marigold Cabs emits about 3,500 trip events per second at peak, each around 1 KiB, from apps that use the AWS SDKs; nobody on the platform team has run Apache Kafka and nobody will be hired to. Three independent teams each need the complete stream at the same time: one lands every event in the company's data lake with no custom code, one computes rolling five-minute trip counts per city for surge pricing within 10 seconds of each event, and a fraud team runs its own service. A late-night batch job once starved the real-time service of read throughput, and the fraud team must be able to re-read the last 12 hours of events after fixing a bug.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
No team's read speed may depend on what any other team is doing
Nothing may run on servers or clusters that the platform team sizes or patches
Finance will not pay for a separate copy of the stream for each team
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented
All three teams can read the complete stream at once at full speed with no team's reads affected by another's, and the fraud team can re-read the last 12 hours of events
Every event lands in the lake with no custom code, and per-city five-minute rolling counts are available within 10 seconds of the event

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
